minutes.headline: Select Board agreed to sign the 64 Chestnut Street boundary agreement without the final plan, and approved aggregation contracts.
minutes.summary: The board edited and approved a water-district grant support letter, renewed the electric aggregation consultant contract and a one-year supply contract, and signed a boundary agreement and release of claims despite concerns that the survey plan was missing. The DPW director presented the four-year residential pavement schedule, and the board ratified a DPW hire. The meeting also covered larger pay-as-you-throw bags, committee reports, and farewells to the departing town manager.

public_comment.topic: Updates: Eagle House renamed Senior Community Center, new programs, fuel assistance, and a Council on Aging letter thanking the town manager.
Frustration over delay of the survey plan; asked the board and town manager to press the surveyor and Town Counsel before a closing a week from Friday.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to execute a boundary line agreement and release of claims for 64 Chestnut Street, though the final survey plan was not yet available.
The board approved the electric aggregation consultant contract extension and a one-year supply contract at a locked-in rate described as near a historic low.
The board authorized the chair to sign a water-district grant support letter, to be redrafted with edits to wording first.
The DPW director presented the four-year residential pavement schedule, and the board ratified a DPW heavy equipment operator appointment.
Year-end transfers were held to the next meeting, and the town manager will look into a thicker 40 gallon pay-as-you-throw bag.

why_it_matters: The aggregation supply contract sets the electricity supply rate for participating households for the next 12 months, and capacity costs are expected to rise next June.

The pavement schedule shows when residential roads are due for work under the debt exclusion voters approved, and any pay-as-you-throw bag change would alter what households pay for trash, not before January 2017.
The boundary agreement releases an insurance claim against the town, so it settles a possible town liability while a public commenter raised the missing survey plan.
watch_next: Year-end budget transfers return at the next Select Board meeting, once the clerical sick leave buyback amounts are settled.
The closing on the 64 Chestnut Street agreement, which a resident said was a week from Friday, and the possible Town Counsel contract agenda item in two weeks.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the motions: the Colonial extension, ConEdison contract, Chestnut Street agreement and Clark appointment all appear in both. Our recording could not hear any vote tallies, so the official minutes supply them. The main difference is the MassWorks letter vote, which the official minutes record as 4–1 with Ebersole opposed and ours leaves blank. Several figures (warrants, MIIA credits, percentage lower) also differ and need checking against the recording.
